attempts.summary: Implemented an Ansible-driven VRRP failover gateway so node3 has a single, always-available address for reaching node4, preferring node1. VyOS routers node1/node2 got static IPs on lan-a (eth1) and lan-b (eth2) plus two VRRP groups (LAN-A vrid10, LAN-B vrid20) sharing virtual IPs 10.60.10.254 and 10.60.20.254; node1 priority 200 (preempting MASTER), node2 priority 100 (BACKUP). node3 and node4 got static addressing plus a single static route to each other's subnet via their local VRRP VIP. Everything was applied and re-verified idempotently through an Ansible playbook (/root/vrrp_gateway.yml + /root/inventory.ini on the node5 control node, run via its run.sh contract). Failover was demonstrated live (disabling then rebooting node1) — node2 took MASTER and node3→node4 ping never dropped — and node1 preempted back to MASTER on recovery. All 5 managed nodes were then restarted one at a time (never more than one router down at once), with boot-id changes proving each restart and post-restart checks confirming VRRP state, interface/IP/route persistence, Ansible re-run idempotency, and unbroken node3↔node4 reachability.
